discovery: Development of massively parallel next-generation DNA sequencing by sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible fluorescent terminators
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes went to protein design and structure prediction (2024) and MOFs (2025), so the committee may turn to bioanalytical chemistry. Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis rests on core chemistry: reversible-terminator nucleotides and cluster amplification on surfaces. It changed biology and medicine, cutting genome costs by roughly a millionfold. The work has already won major awards (the 2020 Breakthrough Prize and the 2022 Millennium Technology Prize), which often come before a Nobel, and it is decades old with clear credit to three people.
